children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares closed higher on Tuesday as preliminary August trade data showed exports extended strong growth, underpinned by artificial-intelligence demand in the chip sector. The won weakened, while the benchmark bond yield rose. ** The benchmark KOSPI

** South Korea on Tuesday unveiled its most aggressive fiscal spending plan on record, setting total government expenditure for 2027 at 821 trillion won ($596.92 billion) to strengthen the country's technological edge amid the global AI race.

** South Korea's exports surged 68.7% in August from a year earlier, extending their winning streak to a 15th consecutive month and outpacing analysts' forecasts as the economy continued to ride a wave of global technology demand.
** Among index heavyweights, chipmaker Samsung Electronics
gained 1.14%. Battery maker LG Energy Solution
were down 0.74% and up 0.15%, respectively. Steelmaker POSCO Holdings

rose 0.13%. ** Of the total 907 traded issues, 446 shares advanced, while 422 declined. ** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 491.9 billion won. ** The won was quoted at 1,370.4 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform

, 0.18% lower than its previous close at 1,368.0. ** The KOSPI has risen 62.21% so far this year. ** The won has strengthened 5.0% against the dollar so far this year. ** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.10 point to 103.13. ** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose 4.1 basis points to 3.878%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
